sentences.text: Tienshanosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — was found near Paikushan in the Shishugou Formation, which dates to the Oxfordian stage.
The known skeleton consists of postcranial elements, while the skull and lower jaws are missing.
The estimated body length of Tienshanosaurus is twelve meters.
Fossilized eggs were found among the sauropod remains discovered in Xinjiang.
Professor Yuan Fuli discovered the remains of approximately thirty adult and three juvenile sauropods in Xinjiang on September 11, 1928.
Paleontologist Yang Zhongjian named the species Tienshanosaurus chitaiensis in 1937.
The generic name Tienshanosaurus refers to the Tian Shan mountains, meaning "heavenly mountains".
The specific name chitaiensis refers to the location Chitai, or Qitai.
Establishing the classification of Tienshanosaurus has been difficult due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil material.
While originally placed in Helopodinae and later various other groups, recent consensus in 2011 assigns Tienshanosaurus to the family Mamenchisauridae.
Tienshanosaurus lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
